d.chapter: Economic Geography — Sectors of the Economy
d.partTitle: Formal and Informal Sectors of the Economy
d.notions: Formal sector, informal sector, taxes, social security (CNPS), registration.
d.focus: The formal and informal sectors of the economy: definitions, characteristics, advantages and problems.
d.competence: Learners are able to tell whether a job around them belongs to the formal or informal sector and explain the advantages of registering a business.
objectives: Define the formal and informal sectors.
Give the characteristics of each sector with examples from Cameroon.
Give the advantages and problems of the informal sector.
recall: The economy has four sectors: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary.
The primary sector extracts, the secondary transforms, the tertiary serves and the quaternary researches.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: difference between a company worker and a street worker.
situation: Mr Bello works for a bank in Garoua. He has a contract, a salary every month and he will receive a pension. His neighbour Moussa is a moto-taxi driver: he has no contract, earns money every day, and has no pension.
One day Moussa falls ill and cannot work for a month. He has no money for his family. His son wonders why his father has no protection like Mr Bello.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Moussa has no money and no protection when he is ill, because he works in the informal sector.
Give two differences between the work of Mr Bello and the work of Moussa.
Mr Bello has a contract and a monthly salary. Moussa has no contract and no pension.
What can Moussa do to be better protected?
He can register with the social security fund (CNPS) as a voluntary member, and save money regularly.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the difference between formal and informal work, which are both very important in Cameroon.

qa.q: A company is registered with the state, pays taxes and declares its workers. What sector does it belong to?
qa.a: It belongs to the formal sector.

qa.q: Give three examples of formal-sector employers in Garoua.
qa.a: Examples are SODECOTON, CICAM, the banks, the hospitals, the schools and the ministries.

sum.title: I. The Formal Sector
defs: The formal sector is the part of the economy made up of activities that are registered with the state, pay taxes and follow the law.
sum.intro: The formal sector has the following characteristics:
items: A. Registration and Taxes
Businesses are registered and pay taxes to the state.
B. Contracts and Salaries
Workers have contracts, regular salaries and fixed working hours.
C. Social Protection
Workers are declared to the social security fund (CNPS) and receive pensions and help in case of accidents.
D. Examples
SODECOTON, CICAM, banks, hospitals, schools and government services are part of the formal sector.

qa.q: Street sellers, moto-taxi drivers and roadside mechanics are not registered and pay few taxes. What sector do they belong to?
qa.a: They belong to the informal sector.

qa.q: Why do so many young people in Cameroon work in the informal sector?
qa.a: It is easy to start, needs little money or diplomas, and there are not enough jobs in the formal sector.

qa.q: Give two problems of working in the informal sector.
qa.a: Workers have no contract, no pension and no protection in case of illness. Their income is irregular.

sum.title: II. The Informal Sector
defs: The informal sector is the part of the economy made up of small activities that are not registered with the state and pay few or no taxes.
sum.intro: The informal sector has the following characteristics:
items: A. Examples
Street selling, moto-taxis, roadside repairs, small shops, hairdressing and small farming are informal activities.
B. Importance
It is easy to start and employs most workers in Cameroon, about nine workers out of ten.
C. Problems
Workers have no contract, no pension and no protection. Their income is irregular, and the state loses taxes.
D. Solutions
The state encourages workers to register their businesses and to join the CNPS, and offers training and small loans.

evaluation: What is the informal sector? Give one example.
The informal sector is made up of small activities that are not registered and pay few taxes, like moto-taxi driving.
Give two advantages of working in the formal sector.
Workers have a regular salary and social protection, such as a pension.
Why does the state want informal workers to register?
It wants them to register so that they pay taxes and receive social protection.
remediation: Activities registered with the state belong to the ______ sector.
Activities not registered with the state belong to the ______ sector.
The social security fund of Cameroon is the ______.
A moto-taxi driver usually works in the ______ sector.
A bank worker works in the ______ sector.
The informal sector employs about ______ workers out of ten in Cameroon.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. formal 2. informal 3. CNPS 4. informal 5. formal 6. nine
d.homework: List four products of farming, fishing, forestry or mining found in the Garoua market, and say where each comes from.
d.homeworkTag: This prepares Part 3: The Primary Sector.
teacherNote: Period 1: recall, situation and part I. Period 2: part II, board summary and evaluation.
Surveys of the National Institute of Statistics (INS, EESI) estimate that close to 90% of workers in Cameroon are in the informal sector.
references: Harmonised Progression Sheet, Economic Geography (5051), Form 2.
Institut National de la Statistique (INS), Enquêtes sur l'Emploi et le Secteur Informel (EESI).
